meta.stack: Vue 3 + Vite + Axios + Vue Router + Pinia
meta.analysis_mode: read-only source inspection; no files modified, no dependencies installed, no tests executed
meta.generated_from: src/api/*.js, src/views/**, src/router/index.js, src/utils/adminErrorMessage.js, src/stores/auth.js, docs/*.md
meta.response_model: For this inventory, response = {status, headers, body}; body is the parsed JSON payload returned by axios interceptor (res.data).

variables.ADMIN_USER_ID: id of an enabled admin account
variables.TEST_APP_ID: existing APPROVED open-platform appId for invalid-transition case
variables.SERVICE_TYPE_ID: existing miniapp service-type id that has at least one service
variables.SHA256_1KB: 64 lowercase hex characters for the 1KB fixture

request_interceptor: Attach Authorization: Bearer <admin_token> when localStorage.admin_token exists.
Remove query params whose value is empty string, undefined, or null.
request_contract.success_envelope: Axios response interceptor returns res.data. Paginated endpoints observed as {items, total}. clientRelease create defensively unwraps {data}.
request_contract.error_envelope: Business errors are expected as response.data.code plus response.data.message. adminErrorMessage.js maps stable codes; HTTP status is fallback.
request_contract.401_policy: For /auth/login, show credential error without redirect. For other endpoints, clear admin_token/admin_user and set hash to #/login.
request_contract.403_policy: Show permission error; no client-side role check exists beyond token presence in router guard.
request_contract.public_request: publicRequest reuses baseURL, sends no Authorization header, unwraps data, and has no 401 redirect interceptor (used by forgot/reset password).

modules.error_handling: No domain error codes in source. All failures pass through request interceptor generic status mapping; page keeps stale/empty list on failure.
TIME_RANGE_INVALID is mapped in adminErrorMessage.js. Other failures use generic status fallback. View resets data to empty on error.

modules.auth: public for login/sso/forgot/reset; Bearer injected when a stale admin_token exists
modules.error_handling: Login 401 is special-cased as credential error. Other 401 clears storage and redirects. 403 shows permission message. SSO codes mapped. publicRequest has no error interceptor, so reset-token failures are surfaced by the page.

modules.auth: bearer; presigned PUT goes directly to object storage without API bearer
modules.error_handling: write() attaches an Idempotency-Key UUID and errorContext. CLIENT_RELEASE_* codes are mapped. Mutations take expectedRowVersion for optimistic concurrency. Upload helper throws local Error if uploadUrl is missing; presigned PUT errors carry plain HTTP status.
No domain error codes. Page catches and logs; request interceptor shows generic message. Batch atomicity is not stated in source.
No domain error codes. Delete errors use resolveAdminErrorMessage in view; list errors use generic interceptor message.
No domain error codes. View clears both friend and user search results on any failure.
No domain error codes. Module has no consumer in src/views; contract is unvalidated by UI.

modules.auth: bearer for API calls; presigned PUT goes directly to object storage
modules.error_handling: Local errors: Invalid media upload request, Media upload was cancelled, Object storage upload failed, missing multipart ETag, Media validation rejected, Media validation timed out (60s at 800ms polling). API errors have no domain codes. Upload session creation/complete use Idempotency-Key.
No domain error codes. List view clears data on failure; trend response shape is not consumed by any view.
No domain error codes. UI blocks duplicate/empty names client-side and states a type with services cannot be deleted, but server error codes are not documented.
No domain error codes. Realtime view logs errors and keeps previous state; end-call failure is shown by interceptor.
No domain error codes in source. UI hides actions by status. appSecret is returned only on approve/reset-secret and displayed once.
No domain error codes in source. UI limits report transitions to pending/processing/resolved/dismissed and treats errors via the global interceptor.
No domain error codes. No view imports this module; server/logs.vue and server/performance.vue use mock data, so the API contract is unvalidated.
No domain error codes. Dashboard catches errors and leaves cards/charts empty.
Delete has documented stable codes: USERNAME_CONFIRM_MISMATCH, ADMIN_ACCOUNT_UNDELETABLE, CANNOT_DELETE_SELF, USER_NOT_FOUND. Other failures use generic interceptor status mapping.

gaps: auth: SSO login, forgot-password happy path, login rate limiting/lockout, and password-reset success are not covered.
user: direct happy-path getUserById, invalid status enum, non-admin 403, self-delete CANNOT_DELETE_SELF, and USER_NOT_FOUND are not covered.
group: group members and dissolveGroup are not covered; the entire module has no UI consumer.
message: no test for pageSize/page upper bounds or invalid enum values.
audit: no test for action/resource/operator combinations, retentionFloor behavior, or pageSize bounds.
config: PUT /admin/config is not covered; batch partial-failure atomicity and unknown configKey handling are unknown.
security: keyword update/delete/toggle, violations list/create, pending count, and valid report transitions (pending->processing->resolved/dismissed) are not covered.
deviceToken: first-delete 404 and pagination bounds are not covered.
userSticker: happy-path delete is not covered.
miniappService: type create/update/sort, service create/delete, link/audience/status validation, and duplicate type name are not covered.
media: upload completion, multipart signatures/part completion, resume, cancel, object status active/rejected/deleted, timeout, checksum mismatch, and presigned PUT are not covered.
monitor: server stats, active/empty call room variants, and concurrent end-call races are not covered.
openPlatform: reset-secret, revoke, reject happy path, and approve on non-PENDING app are not covered.

clientRelease: update, policies, audit logs, platforms, rollout, pause, resume, withdraw, archive, preview artifact upload, invalid SemVer/SHA-256, platform-not-enabled, download-host rejection, and not-found are not covered.
server: metrics and nodes are not covered; no UI consumer exists for this module.
stats: time-series trend and days boundary are not covered.
accountCancellation: log-detail, log search, status filters, and missing-parent behavior are not covered.
Cross-cutting: no 403 authorization case, no 429 rate-limit case, no 15s timeout case, no request-size limit, no CORS/CSRF, no XSS/injection, and no audit-trail assertion after mutations.
risks: No OpenAPI or backend contract exists in the repository. Success envelopes, HTTP statuses, and field names are inferred from axios usage and Vue templates; 12 of 18 modules have no documented error code.
Only 14 stable error codes are visible, all in src/utils/adminErrorMessage.js. Eight error cases therefore assert code presence rather than a specific code, which reduces oracle strength.
Authentication is token-presence-only in the router. The source says admin role is required but exposes no role/permission matrix, so 403 semantics and tenant isolation cannot be derived from source.
group and server are unconsumed API modules; server/logs.vue and server/performance.vue use mocks. Endpoints may be absent, renamed, or contract-drifted without any UI signal.

Media and client-release artifact uploads use presigned object-storage URLs outside the API base. Reliable execution needs a real bucket, CORS, ETag exposure, and cleanup policy not present in source.

Idempotency semantics are undocumented: clientRelease write() generates a new UUID per call, while media generates UUIDs per create/complete. Replay window, cached response, and conflict behavior are assumptions encoded in TC-020, TC-030, and TC-037.
Optimistic concurrency depends on expectedRowVersion. How clients obtain the current value and which conflict code is returned for a stale version are not specified beyond CLIENT_RELEASE_* messages.
TC-029 assumes /monitor/online/users returns the complete online set. If the endpoint caps or paginates the list, count equality is a false oracle.
TC-018 assumes resolved reports cannot transition back to pending. That rule is inferred from UI action visibility, not backend validation.

Shared mutable fixtures are required for user status, config batch, release lifecycle, and open-platform approval. There is no release-delete endpoint, and approve cannot be reversed to PENDING without DB reset.
Time handling is split: audit from/to use YYYY-MM-DD, client-release scheduledAt is converted to UTC. Boundary tests can be flaky around midnight/time zones.
Pagination bounds, enum validation, and empty-parameter behavior are not documented. The interceptor silently strips empty query params, which can hide invalid-input bugs.
Sensitive data handling must be explicit: appSecret is one-time, device tokens must expose only fingerprints, and test logs must not persist either.
The 20MB multipart threshold is client-side. Server part size and threshold may differ; TC-027 asserts internal self-consistency rather than a fixed server part size.
The 401 interceptor clears storage and redirects to #/login. UI-driven tests can lose session mid-suite; HTTP-level tests are safer.
Source-parsing alone cannot distinguish unused API wrappers from real supported endpoints, so coverage percentage overstates behavioral confidence.

assessment.summary: Source parsing is sufficient to build a high-quality request inventory and an executable skeleton for 40 cases across all 18 API modules, but it is not sufficient to make the suite reliable or comprehensive. The repository exposes request construction, UI usage, and a small error-code vocabulary, yet omits the backend contract, fixtures, role matrix, idempotency semantics, and upload-bucket behavior needed for trustworthy oracles.
what_source_parsing_yields: 18 API modules and 87 HTTP touchpoints with method, path, parameters, auth mode, response shape hints, and source line numbers.
Global request behavior: Bearer injection, X-Client headers, empty-query stripping, 15s timeout, 401 redirect policy, and publicRequest behavior.
UI-derived field names, list envelope {items,total}, status enums, and 14 stable error codes across user, audit, auth/SSO, and client release.
Enough structure to generate 40 cases with deterministic request payloads, preconditions, cleanup, and assertions that are executable once fixtures exist.
Clear dead-code and mock signals: group is unreferenced; server is unreferenced while server views use mocks, lowering confidence in those contracts.
what_source_parsing_cannot_yield: Authoritative success/error envelopes, exact HTTP status mapping, and error codes for 12 of 18 modules.
Role/permission matrix, tenant isolation rules, and 403 behavior.
Idempotency replay semantics, concurrency conflict codes, and whether expectedRowVersion uses body or header.
Presigned object-storage behavior, bucket CORS, ETag exposure, multipart part sizing, and cleanup APIs.
Test fixtures, database reset hooks, seed data, and safe lifecycle management for irreversible transitions.
Pagination bounds, enum validation, duplicate constraints, and numeric limits not represented in UI code.
Which unconsumed endpoints are actually supported and which are leftovers.
assessment.confidence: medium for request inventory; low-to-medium for assertions on modules without documented error codes or UI consumers
recommended_next_inputs: Backend OpenAPI/route schema, response envelope, status-code table, and complete stable error-code registry.
Seed/fixture API or database snapshot with deterministic admin, user, group, report, call, release, app, and media records.
Role/permission matrix including non-admin and cross-tenant negative cases.
Idempotency and optimistic-concurrency contract, including replay window and conflict codes.
Object-storage test bucket credentials, CORS policy, ETag policy, and cleanup job.
Mock-server or contract-test layer for the two dead modules and for presigned upload flows.
